FRIDAY, OCTOBER 16, 2026

Community Grief Ritual: Tending the Soil

6:00 PM – 9:00 PM MDT

Boulder

Facilitated by Danielle Rifkin, Dan Maynard, and Sarah (Naiya) D'Antoni of the Grief Collective. Positioned at the opening of Cohere week, this ritual seeds the soil for what the week will grow. Before we can plant connection, we have to grieve where we fractured: where we lost each other, where ruptures went unrepaired, where survival under capitalism pulled us away from each other, where we got severed from land. We grieve alone because we forgot how to grieve together. This ritual is a return to the village, a remembering that mourning was always meant to be collective. We'll work with song, story, and systemic constellations, drawing on ritual lineages from Joanna Macy, Francis Weller, Martin Prechtel, Malidoma Somé, and the Mythic Body.

SATURDAY, OCTOBER 17, 2026

Mindful Birding Walk at High Plains Environmental Center

9:00 AM – 11:30 AM MDT

High Plains Environmental Center · 2698 Bluestem Willow Dr · Loveland

A mindful birding walk combines traditional birdwatching with mindfulness techniques, focusing on slow-paced, intentional awareness of birds and nature. Observing birds in their natural habitat can be inspiring and relaxing while also offering a variety of health benefits. This way of connecting with nature encourages purposeful curiosity, builds community, and deepens our appreciation for birds and the natural world. Join us at the High Plains Environmental Center to explore mindfulness and birds and learn simple techniques you can take home and practice on your own. We’ll begin in the classroom and then head outside for a guided walk. All abilities and interests are welcome! We'll provide bird books and binoculars. Please dress appropriately for the weather. Registration: Sign-up information will be available in September. We will notify registered participants of any changes due to weather or other circumstances.

MONDAY, OCTOBER 19, 2026

A Sound Healing Journey into the Womb of the Earth for Ecological Self-Restoration

8:00 AM – 9:30 AM MDT

Eben G Fine Park · Boulder

Facilitated by Ayleen Guzman of Mamafaeria Healing Arts At the center of this offering is the understanding that the Earth is not simply the place where we live, but a living spiritual presence that can become a gateway into connection with the Divine, the Divine Mother, God, our ancestors, and ourselves. The womb of the Earth can become a place of return, remembrance, healing, and transformation. We are living through profound and rapidly changing times. Across many Indigenous, African, Native, and spiritual traditions, there are teachings about periods of great transformation in which humanity is called to remember its relationship with the Earth and return to right relationship with one another. Within my own spiritual framework, this is a time when the Earth is calling us to become more sensitive to her presence, her needs, and the wisdom she carries. The intention of this ceremony is to begin cultivating that relationship consciously.

MONDAY, OCTOBER 19, 2026

People of the Sacred Land (Film Screening + Dialogue)

5:30 PM – 7:30 PM MDT

Naropa Cultural Center · 2150 Arapahoe Ave · Boulder

The Untold History of Colorado The idea that we are living on stolen land isn’t new, or even novel; it’s a reality that exists across settler communities worldwide, and many people in the United States are aware of the blatant agendas, coercion, and profound immorality of the treaty process. What’s often missing from that conversation, however, are rigorous, comprehensive, academically supported Native-led studies proving that— even through the lens of modern law— large areas of what we call the United States remain illegally occupied. And nowhere is the evidence and culpability more dramatic than in the state of Colorado. PEOPLE of the SACRED LAND (2026, 32 min) follows Richard Willams (Oglala Lakota, Northern Cheyenne) as he recounts the findings of the Truth, Restoration, and Education Commission (TREC) of Colorado’s TREC Reports. While Rick’s story focuses on Colorado, the approach, implications, and impact of his work provide a model for Native leaders across the continent. Richard Williams: Executive Producer Dewi: Director, cinematographer, editor Sarah Ortegon Highwalking: Field director Jason: Cinematographer, finishing editor

Caring for families who care for families

10:00 AM – 12:00 PM MDT

Martin Park · 3600 Eastman Ave · Boulder

This event is a meet and greet for families and those feeling called to support families in a deeper way. We will get to know one another, share our dreams, challenges, and needs...and enjoy the time outside while little ones run around the park (with support!). 2:00 PM – 3:30 PM MDT

Canyon Theater @ Boulder Public Library · 1000 Canyon Blvd · Boulder

Through monologues, film, and live music, Uprooting Qahr! Power, Privilege, and Paperwork, follows Taishya Adams - educator, artist, and policymaker - as she shares personal and political narratives that confront the colonial cancer that spread from Europe to Africa, the Americas and West Asia. Weaving across time and space, we face the uneven promise of democracy and the possibilities of liberty and justice for all. What is COhere?

COhere Boulder stokes Boulder's culture and engagement by connecting residents, organizations, artists, leaders, and innovators during a 10-day container. Through a curated calendar of values-aligned events and memorable opening & closing gatherings, we strengthen community ties, highlight our city's vibrancy, and inspire action toward a more regenerative, resilient future.

This isn't just another conference or workshop series. It's a carefully designed journey that helps our community discover its own resilience patterns, strengthen existing connections, and create new pathways for collaboration.

Building on the success of COhere 2024 and 2025, we're evolving into an annual rhythm that makes community participation memorable, meaningful, and accessible to all.

THIS YEAR'S THEME

We Are Our Ecology

The Community Calendar

Co-created by everyone who shows up

COhere doesn't program the ten days from the top down. Every event on the calendar is offered by someone in this community — a dinner, a walk, a workshop, a song circle, a conversation that needed a room.

Browse what's unfolding, and if you're holding something you'd like to share, there's room for it here.

Explore the Calendar
Co-create
Choose Your Own Adventure

There is no single way to do COhere. Ten days, a calendar the community builds together, and an open invitation to find your own thread through it.

Come to one gathering or a dozen. Host something. Bring a friend. Meet the people already tending what you care about — and find your role in the web.

Participate

We hope all participants build new relationships, learn meaningful things about Boulder, and find their role in the web.

Contribute

Share a story, host an event, volunteer, make art.

Lead

Get involved in the organizing team, or anchor an element of COhere that brings a dimension of community to life.

Experience COhere

See and feel what COhere is all about — films from our first two years

COhere Boulder

COhere 2024 Recap

Two years of weaving: hundreds of community members and dozens of co-created events across Boulder, strengthening connections and planting seeds for our regenerative future.

The Spirit of COhere
Active Participation

Life becomes more meaningful when we lean in, being courageously participatory

Radical Interdependence

Be bold with offers and requests—discover what's possible when we lean on each other

Anchor Abundance

Give generously and trust that collectively, we are resourced for all to thrive

"The journey of weaving our resilience never begins and never ends. COhere is simply a rhythm that calls deeper attention to this process in which we all engage."

Boulder's Regenerative Ecosystem

Together with Climatique, we created this map to demonstrate the rich tapestry of projects and groups working towards regenerative change in our community.

Explore the Map
Suggest Additions
Join the Weaving

COhere is for everyone who cares about Boulder's future and wants to be part of creating a more connected, resilient community.

Whether you participate in events, offer your gifts, or simply embody the spirit of COhere in daily life, you're part of this weaving.

FRIDAY, OCTOBER 16, 2026

Community Grief Ritual: Tending the Soil

6:00 PM – 9:00 PM MDT

Boulder

Facilitated by Danielle Rifkin, Dan Maynard, and Sarah (Naiya) D'Antoni of the Grief Collective. Positioned at the opening of Cohere week, this ritual seeds the soil for what the week will grow. Before we can plant connection, we have to grieve where we fractured: where we lost each other, where ruptures went unrepaired, where survival under capitalism pulled us away from each other, where we got severed from land. We grieve alone because we forgot how to grieve together. This ritual is a return to the village, a remembering that mourning was always meant to be collective. We'll work with song, story, and systemic constellations, drawing on ritual lineages from Joanna Macy, Francis Weller, Martin Prechtel, Malidoma Somé, and the Mythic Body.

A mindful birding walk combines traditional birdwatching with mindfulness techniques, focusing on slow-paced, intentional awareness of birds and nature. This way of connecting with nature encourages purposeful curiosity, builds community, and deepens our appreciation for birds and the natural world. Join us at the High Plains Environmental Center to explore mindfulness and birds and learn simple techniques you can take home and practice on your own. We’ll begin in the classroom and then head outside for a guided walk. All abilities and interests are welcome! We'll provide bird books and binoculars. Please dress appropriately for the weather. Community Grief Ritual: Tending the Soil

18:00 – 21:00 GMT-6

Boulder

Facilitated by Danielle Rifkin, Dan Maynard, and Sarah (Naiya) D'Antoni of the Grief Collective. Positioned at the opening of Cohere week, this ritual seeds the soil for what the week will grow. Before we can plant connection, we have to grieve where we fractured: where we lost each other, where ruptures went unrepaired, where survival under capitalism pulled us away from each other, where we got severed from land. We grieve alone because we forgot how to grieve together. This ritual is a return to the village, a remembering that mourning was always meant to be collective. We'll work with song, story, and systemic constellations, drawing on ritual lineages from Joanna Macy, Francis Weller, Martin Prechtel, Malidoma Somé, and the Mythic Body.

Eben G Fine Park · Boulder

Facilitated by Ayleen Guzman of Mamafaeria Healing Arts At the center of this offering is the understanding that the Earth is not simply the place where we live, but a living spiritual presence that can become a gateway into connection with the Divine, the Divine Mother, God, our ancestors, and ourselves. The womb of the Earth can become a place of return, remembrance, healing, and transformation. We are living through profound and rapidly changing times. The intention of this ceremony is to begin cultivating that relationship consciously.

LUNES, 19 DE OCTUBRE DE 2026

People of the Sacred Land (Film Screening + Dialogue)

17:30 – 19:30 GMT-6

Naropa Cultural Center · 2150 Arapahoe Ave · Boulder

The Untold History of Colorado The idea that we are living on stolen land isn’t new, or even novel; it’s a reality that exists across settler communities worldwide, and many people in the United States are aware of the blatant agendas, coercion, and profound immorality of the treaty process. What’s often missing from that conversation, however, are rigorous, comprehensive, academically supported Native-led studies proving that— even through the lens of modern law— large areas of what we call the United States remain illegally occupied. And nowhere is the evidence and culpability more dramatic than in the state of Colorado. PEOPLE of the SACRED LAND (2026, 32 min) follows Richard Willams (Oglala Lakota, Northern Cheyenne) as he recounts the findings of the Truth, Restoration, and Education Commission (TREC) of Colorado’s TREC Reports. While Rick’s story focuses on Colorado, the approach, implications, and impact of his work provide a model for Native leaders across the continent. Richard Williams: Executive Producer Dewi: Director, cinematographer, editor Sarah Ortegon Highwalking: Field director Jason: Cinematographer, finishing editor

People of the Sacred Land (Film Screening + Dialogue)

17:30 – 19:30 GMT-6

Naropa Cultural Center · 2150 Arapahoe Ave · Boulder

The Untold History of Colorado The idea that we are living on stolen land isn’t new, or even novel; it’s a reality that exists across settler communities worldwide, and many people in the United States are aware of the blatant agendas, coercion, and profound immorality of the treaty process. What’s often missing from that conversation, however, are rigorous, comprehensive, academically supported Native-led studies proving that— even through the lens of modern law— large areas of what we call the United States remain illegally occupied. And nowhere is the evidence and culpability more dramatic than in the state of Colorado. PEOPLE of the SACRED LAND (2026, 32 min) follows Richard Willams (Oglala Lakota, Northern Cheyenne) as he recounts the findings of the Truth, Restoration, and Education Commission (TREC) of Colorado’s TREC Reports. While Rick’s story focuses on Colorado, the approach, implications, and impact of his work provide a model for Native leaders across the continent. Richard Williams: Executive Producer Dewi: Director, cinematographer, editor Sarah Ortegon Highwalking: Field director Jason: Cinematographer, finishing editor

Before we can plant connection, we have to grieve where we fractured: where we lost each other, where ruptures went unrepaired, where survival under capitalism pulled us away from each other, where we got severed from land. We'll work with song, story, and systemic constellations, drawing on ritual lineages from Joanna Macy, Francis Weller, Martin Prechtel, Malidoma Somé, and the Mythic Body.

¿Qué es COhere?

COhere Boulder aviva la cultura y el compromiso de Boulder conectando residentes, organizaciones, artistas, líderes e innovadores durante un contenedor de 10 días. A través de un calendario curado de eventos alineados con valores y reuniones memorables de apertura y cierre, fortalecemos los lazos comunitarios, destacamos la vitalidad de nuestra ciudad e inspiramos acción hacia un futuro más regenerativo y resiliente.

Esto no es solo otra conferencia o serie de talleres. Es un viaje cuidadosamente diseñado que ayuda a nuestra comunidad a descubrir sus propios patrones de resiliencia, fortalecer las conexiones existentes y crear nuevos caminos para la colaboración.

Basándonos en el éxito de COhere 2024 y 2025, estamos evolucionando hacia un ritmo anual que hace que la participación comunitaria sea memorable, significativa y accesible para todos.

EL TEMA DE ESTE AÑO

Somos Nuestra Ecología

El calendario comunitario

Co-creado por todas las personas que participan

COhere no programa los diez días desde arriba. Cada evento del calendario es ofrecido por alguien de esta comunidad: una cena, una caminata, un taller, un círculo de canto, una conversación que necesitaba un espacio.

Explora lo que se está desplegando y, si tienes algo que quieras compartir, aquí hay espacio para ello.

Explorar el Calendario
Co-crear
Elige Tu Propia Aventura

No hay una sola manera de vivir COhere. Diez días, un calendario que la comunidad construye en conjunto y una invitación abierta a encontrar tu propio hilo.

Ven a un encuentro o a doce. Organiza algo. Trae a alguien. Conoce a las personas que ya cuidan lo que te importa y encuentra tu lugar en la red.

Participa

Esperamos que todas las personas participantes creen nuevas relaciones, aprendan cosas significativas sobre Boulder y encuentren su lugar en la red.

Contribuye

Comparte una historia, organiza un evento, ofrece tu tiempo, crea arte.

Lidera

Súmate al equipo organizador o ancla un elemento de COhere que dé vida a una dimensión de la comunidad.

Experimenta COhere

Mira y siente de qué se trata COhere — películas de nuestros primeros dos años

COhere Boulder

Resumen de COhere 2024

Dos años de tejido: cientos de miembros de la comunidad y docenas de eventos co-creados en todo Boulder, fortaleciendo conexiones y plantando semillas para nuestro futuro regenerativo.

El Espíritu de COhere
Participación Activa

La vida se vuelve más significativa cuando nos involucramos, siendo valientemente participativos

Interdependencia Radical

Sé audaz con ofertas y solicitudes: descubre lo que es posible cuando nos apoyamos mutuamente

Anclar la Abundancia

Da generosamente y confía en que colectivamente, tenemos recursos para que todos prosperen

"El viaje de tejer nuestra resiliencia nunca comienza ni termina. COhere es simplemente un ritmo que llama a prestar mayor atención a este proceso en el que todos participamos."

Ecosistema Regenerativo de Boulder

Junto con Climatique, creamos este mapa para demostrar el rico tapiz de proyectos y grupos que trabajan hacia el cambio regenerativo en nuestra comunidad.

Explora el Mapa
Sugerir Adiciones
Únete al Tejido

COhere es para todos los que se preocupan por el futuro de Boulder y quieren ser parte de crear una comunidad más conectada y resiliente.

Ya sea que participes en eventos, ofrezcas tus dones, o simplemente encarnes el espíritu de COhere en la vida diaria, eres parte de este tejido.

Resumen de COhere 2024

Dos años de tejido: cientos de miembros de la comunidad y docenas de eventos co-creados en todo Boulder, fortaleciendo conexiones y plantando semillas para nuestro futuro regenerativo.

El Espíritu de COhere
Participación Activa

La vida se vuelve más significativa cuando nos involucramos, siendo valientemente participativos

Interdependencia Radical

Sé audaz con ofertas y solicitudes: descubre lo que es posible cuando nos apoyamos mutuamente

Anclar la Abundancia

Da generosamente y confía en que colectivamente, tenemos recursos para que todos prosperen

"El viaje de tejer nuestra resiliencia nunca comienza ni termina. COhere es simplemente un ritmo que llama a prestar mayor atención a este proceso en el que todos participamos."

Ecosistema Regenerativo de Boulder

Junto con Climatique, creamos este mapa para demostrar el rico tapiz de proyectos y grupos que trabajan hacia el cambio regenerativo en nuestra comunidad.

Explora el Mapa

Únete al Tejido

COhere es para todos los que se preocupan por el futuro de Boulder y quieren ser parte de crear una comunidad más conectada y resiliente.

Ya sea que participes en eventos, ofrezcas tus dones, o simplemente encarnes el espíritu de COhere en la vida diaria, eres parte de este tejido.

Community Grief Ritual: Tending the Soil

18:00 – 21:00 GMT-6

Boulder

Facilitated by Danielle Rifkin, Dan Maynard, and Sarah (Naiya) D'Antoni of the Grief Collective. Positioned at the opening of Cohere week, this ritual seeds the soil for what the week will grow. Before we can plant connection, we have to grieve where we fractured: where we lost each other, where ruptures went unrepaired, where survival under capitalism pulled us away from each other, where we got severed from land. We grieve alone because we forgot how to grieve together. This ritual is a return to the village, a remembering that mourning was always meant to be collective. We'll work with song, story, and systemic constellations, drawing on ritual lineages from Joanna Macy, Francis Weller, Martin Prechtel, Malidoma Somé, and the Mythic Body.

LUNES, 19 DE OCTUBRE DE 2026

A Sound Healing Journey into the Womb of the Earth for Ecological Self-Restoration

8:00 – 9:30 GMT-6

Eben G Fine Park · Boulder

Facilitated by Ayleen Guzman of Mamafaeria Healing Arts At the center of this offering is the understanding that the Earth is not simply the place where we live, but a living spiritual presence that can become a gateway into connection with the Divine, the Divine Mother, God, our ancestors, and ourselves. The womb of the Earth can become a place of return, remembrance, healing, and transformation. We are living through profound and rapidly changing times. Across many Indigenous, African, Native, and spiritual traditions, there are teachings about periods of great transformation in which humanity is called to remember its relationship with the Earth and return to right relationship with one another. Within my own spiritual framework, this is a time when the Earth is calling us to become more sensitive to her presence, her needs, and the wisdom she carries. The intention of this ceremony is to begin cultivating that relationship consciously.

LUNES, 19 DE OCTUBRE DE 2026

People of the Sacred Land (Film Screening + Dialogue)

17:30 – 19:30 GMT-6

Naropa Cultural Center · 2150 Arapahoe Ave · Boulder

The Untold History of Colorado The idea that we are living on stolen land isn’t new, or even novel; it’s a reality that exists across settler communities worldwide, and many people in the United States are aware of the blatant agendas, coercion, and profound immorality of the treaty process. What’s often missing from that conversation, however, are rigorous, comprehensive, academically supported Native-led studies proving that— even through the lens of modern law— large areas of what we call the United States remain illegally occupied. And nowhere is the evidence and culpability more dramatic than in the state of Colorado. PEOPLE of the SACRED LAND (2026, 32 min) follows Richard Willams (Oglala Lakota, Northern Cheyenne) as he recounts the findings of the Truth, Restoration, and Education Commission (TREC) of Colorado’s TREC Reports. While Rick’s story focuses on Colorado, the approach, implications, and impact of his work provide a model for Native leaders across the continent. Richard Williams: Executive Producer Dewi: Director, cinematographer, editor Sarah Ortegon Highwalking: Field director Jason: Cinematographer, finishing editor

The Untold History of Colorado The idea that we are living on stolen land isn’t new, or even novel; it’s a reality that exists across settler communities worldwide, and many people in the United States are aware of the blatant agendas, coercion, and profound immorality of the treaty process. What’s often missing from that conversation, however, are rigorous, comprehensive, academically supported Native-led studies proving that— even through the lens of modern law— large areas of what we call the United States remain illegally occupied. FRIDAY, OCTOBER 16, 2026

Community Grief Ritual: Tending the Soil

6:00 PM – 9:00 PM MDT

Boulder

Facilitated by Danielle Rifkin, Dan Maynard, and Sarah (Naiya) D'Antoni of the Grief Collective. Positioned at the opening of Cohere week, this ritual seeds the soil for what the week will grow. Before we can plant connection, we have to grieve where we fractured: where we lost each other, where ruptures went unrepaired, where survival under capitalism pulled us away from each other, where we got severed from land. We grieve alone because we forgot how to grieve together. This ritual is a return to the village, a remembering that mourning was always meant to be collective. We'll work with song, story, and systemic constellations, drawing on ritual lineages from Joanna Macy, Francis Weller, Martin Prechtel, Malidoma Somé, and the Mythic Body.

FRIDAY, OCTOBER 16, 2026

Community Grief Ritual: Tending the Soil

6:00 PM – 9:00 PM MDT

Boulder

Facilitated by Danielle Rifkin, Dan Maynard, and Sarah (Naiya) D'Antoni of the Grief Collective. Positioned at the opening of Cohere week, this ritual seeds the soil for what the week will grow. Before we can plant connection, we have to grieve where we fractured: where we lost each other, where ruptures went unrepaired, where survival under capitalism pulled us away from each other, where we got severed from land. We grieve alone because we forgot how to grieve together. This ritual is a return to the village, a remembering that mourning was always meant to be collective. We'll work with song, story, and systemic constellations, drawing on ritual lineages from Joanna Macy, Francis Weller, Martin Prechtel, Malidoma Somé, and the Mythic Body.

A mindful birding walk combines traditional birdwatching with mindfulness techniques, focusing on slow-paced, intentional awareness of birds and nature. People of the Sacred Land (Film Screening + Dialogue)

5:30 PM – 7:30 PM MDT

Naropa Cultural Center · 2150 Arapahoe Ave · Boulder

The Untold History of Colorado The idea that we are living on stolen land isn’t new, or even novel; it’s a reality that exists across settler communities worldwide, and many people in the United States are aware of the blatant agendas, coercion, and profound immorality of the treaty process. What’s often missing from that conversation, however, are rigorous, comprehensive, academically supported Native-led studies proving that— even through the lens of modern law— large areas of what we call the United States remain illegally occupied. And nowhere is the evidence and culpability more dramatic than in the state of Colorado. PEOPLE of the SACRED LAND (2026, 32 min) follows Richard Willams (Oglala Lakota, Northern Cheyenne) as he recounts the findings of the Truth, Restoration, and Education Commission (TREC) of Colorado’s TREC Reports. While Rick’s story focuses on Colorado, the approach, implications, and impact of his work provide a model for Native leaders across the continent. Richard Williams: Executive Producer Dewi: Director, cinematographer, editor Sarah Ortegon Highwalking: Field director Jason: Cinematographer, finishing editor

What is COhere?

COhere Boulder stokes Boulder's culture and engagement by connecting residents, organizations, artists, leaders, and innovators during a 10-day container. Through a curated calendar of values-aligned events and memorable opening & closing gatherings, we strengthen community ties, highlight our city's vibrancy, and inspire action toward a more regenerative, resilient future.

This isn't just another conference or workshop series. It's a carefully designed journey that helps our community discover its own resilience patterns, strengthen existing connections, and create new pathways for collaboration.

Building on the success of COhere 2024 and 2025, we're evolving into an annual rhythm that makes community participation memorable, meaningful, and accessible to all.

THIS YEAR'S THEME

We Are Our Ecology

The Community Calendar

Co-created by everyone who shows up

COhere doesn't program the ten days from the top down. Every event on the calendar is offered by someone in this community — a dinner, a walk, a workshop, a song circle, a conversation that needed a room.

Browse what's unfolding, and if you're holding something you'd like to share, there's room for it here.

Explore the Calendar
Co-create
Choose Your Own Adventure

There is no single way to do COhere. Ten days, a calendar the community builds together, and an open invitation to find your own thread through it.

Come to one gathering or a dozen. Host something. Bring a friend. Meet the people already tending what you care about — and find your role in the web.

Participate

We hope all participants build new relationships, learn meaningful things about Boulder, and find their role in the web.

Contribute

Share a story, host an event, volunteer, make art.

Lead

Get involved in the organizing team, or anchor an element of COhere that brings a dimension of community to life.

Experience COhere

See and feel what COhere is all about — films from our first two years

COhere Boulder

COhere 2024 Recap

Two years of weaving: hundreds of community members and dozens of co-created events across Boulder, strengthening connections and planting seeds for our regenerative future.

The Spirit of COhere
Active Participation

Life becomes more meaningful when we lean in, being courageously participatory

Radical Interdependence

Be bold with offers and requests—discover what's possible when we lean on each other

Anchor Abundance

Give generously and trust that collectively, we are resourced for all to thrive

"The journey of weaving our resilience never begins and never ends. COhere is simply a rhythm that calls deeper attention to this process in which we all engage."

Boulder's Regenerative Ecosystem

Together with Climatique, we created this map to demonstrate the rich tapestry of projects and groups working towards regenerative change in our community.

Explore the Map
Suggest Additions
Join the Weaving

COhere is for everyone who cares about Boulder's future and wants to be part of creating a more connected, resilient community.

Whether you participate in events, offer your gifts, or simply embody the spirit of COhere in daily life, you're part of this weaving.

A Sound Healing Journey into the Womb of the Earth for Ecological Self-Restoration

8:00 AM – 9:30 AM MDT

Eben G Fine Park · Boulder

Facilitated by Ayleen Guzman of Mamafaeria Healing Arts At the center of this offering is the understanding that the Earth is not simply the place where we live, but a living spiritual presence that can become a gateway into connection with the Divine, the Divine Mother, God, our ancestors, and ourselves. The womb of the Earth can become a place of return, remembrance, healing, and transformation. We are living through profound and rapidly changing times. Across many Indigenous, African, Native, and spiritual traditions, there are teachings about periods of great transformation in which humanity is called to remember its relationship with the Earth and return to right relationship with one another. Within my own spiritual framework, this is a time when the Earth is calling us to become more sensitive to her presence, her needs, and the wisdom she carries. The intention of this ceremony is to begin cultivating that relationship consciously.

MONDAY, OCTOBER 19, 2026

People of the Sacred Land (Film Screening + Dialogue)

5:30 PM – 7:30 PM MDT

Naropa Cultural Center · 2150 Arapahoe Ave · Boulder

The Untold History of Colorado The idea that we are living on stolen land isn’t new, or even novel; it’s a reality that exists across settler communities worldwide, and many people in the United States are aware of the blatant agendas, coercion, and profound immorality of the treaty process. What’s often missing from that conversation, however, are rigorous, comprehensive, academically supported Native-led studies proving that— even through the lens of modern law— large areas of what we call the United States remain illegally occupied. And nowhere is the evidence and culpability more dramatic than in the state of Colorado. PEOPLE of the SACRED LAND (2026, 32 min) follows Richard Willams (Oglala Lakota, Northern Cheyenne) as he recounts the findings of the Truth, Restoration, and Education Commission (TREC) of Colorado’s TREC Reports. While Rick’s story focuses on Colorado, the approach, implications, and impact of his work provide a model for Native leaders across the continent. Richard Williams: Executive Producer Dewi: Director, cinematographer, editor Sarah Ortegon Highwalking: Field director Jason: Cinematographer, finishing editor

People of the Sacred Land (Film Screening + Dialogue)

5:30 PM – 7:30 PM MDT

Naropa Cultural Center · 2150 Arapahoe Ave · Boulder

The Untold History of Colorado The idea that we are living on stolen land isn’t new, or even novel; it’s a reality that exists across settler communities worldwide, and many people in the United States are aware of the blatant agendas, coercion, and profound immorality of the treaty process. What’s often missing from that conversation, however, are rigorous, comprehensive, academically supported Native-led studies proving that— even through the lens of modern law— large areas of what we call the United States remain illegally occupied. And nowhere is the evidence and culpability more dramatic than in the state of Colorado. PEOPLE of the SACRED LAND (2026, 32 min) follows Richard Willams (Oglala Lakota, Northern Cheyenne) as he recounts the findings of the Truth, Restoration, and Education Commission (TREC) of Colorado’s TREC Reports. While Rick’s story focuses on Colorado, the approach, implications, and impact of his work provide a model for Native leaders across the continent. The Untold History of Colorado The idea that we are living on stolen land isn’t new, or even novel; it’s a reality that exists across settler communities worldwide, and many people in the United States are aware of the blatant agendas, coercion, and profound immorality of the treaty process. PEOPLE of the SACRED LAND (2026, 32 min) follows Richard Willams (Oglala Lakota, Northern Cheyenne) as he recounts the findings of the Truth, Restoration, and Education Commission (TREC) of Colorado’s TREC Reports. Community Grief Ritual: Tending the Soil

18:00 – 21:00 GMT-6

Boulder

Facilitated by Danielle Rifkin, Dan Maynard, and Sarah (Naiya) D'Antoni of the Grief Collective. Positioned at the opening of Cohere week, this ritual seeds the soil for what the week will grow. Before we can plant connection, we have to grieve where we fractured: where we lost each other, where ruptures went unrepaired, where survival under capitalism pulled us away from each other, where we got severed from land. We grieve alone because we forgot how to grieve together. This ritual is a return to the village, a remembering that mourning was always meant to be collective. We'll work with song, story, and systemic constellations, drawing on ritual lineages from Joanna Macy, Francis Weller, Martin Prechtel, Malidoma Somé, and the Mythic Body.

¿Qué es COhere?

COhere Boulder aviva la cultura y el compromiso de Boulder conectando residentes, organizaciones, artistas, líderes e innovadores durante un contenedor de 10 días. A través de un calendario curado de eventos alineados con valores y reuniones memorables de apertura y cierre, fortalecemos los lazos comunitarios, destacamos la vitalidad de nuestra ciudad e inspiramos acción hacia un futuro más regenerativo y resiliente.

Esto no es solo otra conferencia o serie de talleres. Es un viaje cuidadosamente diseñado que ayuda a nuestra comunidad a descubrir sus propios patrones de resiliencia, fortalecer las conexiones existentes y crear nuevos caminos para la colaboración.

Basándonos en el éxito de COhere 2024 y 2025, estamos evolucionando hacia un ritmo anual que hace que la participación comunitaria sea memorable, significativa y accesible para todos.

EL TEMA DE ESTE AÑO

Somos Nuestra Ecología

El calendario comunitario

Co-creado por todas las personas que participan

COhere no programa los diez días desde arriba. Cada evento del calendario es ofrecido por alguien de esta comunidad: una cena, una caminata, un taller, un círculo de canto, una conversación que necesitaba un espacio.

Explora lo que se está desplegando y, si tienes algo que quieras compartir, aquí hay espacio para ello.

Explorar el Calendario
Co-crear
Elige Tu Propia Aventura

No hay una sola manera de vivir COhere. Diez días, un calendario que la comunidad construye en conjunto y una invitación abierta a encontrar tu propio hilo.

Ven a un encuentro o a doce. Organiza algo. Trae a alguien. Conoce a las personas que ya cuidan lo que te importa y encuentra tu lugar en la red.

Participa

Esperamos que todas las personas participantes creen nuevas relaciones, aprendan cosas significativas sobre Boulder y encuentren su lugar en la red.

Contribuye

Comparte una historia, organiza un evento, ofrece tu tiempo, crea arte.

Lidera

Súmate al equipo organizador o ancla un elemento de COhere que dé vida a una dimensión de la comunidad.

Experimenta COhere

Mira y siente de qué se trata COhere — películas de nuestros primeros dos años

COhere Boulder

Resumen de COhere 2024

Dos años de tejido: cientos de miembros de la comunidad y docenas de eventos co-creados en todo Boulder, fortaleciendo conexiones y plantando semillas para nuestro futuro regenerativo.

El Espíritu de COhere
Participación Activa

La vida se vuelve más significativa cuando nos involucramos, siendo valientemente participativos

Interdependencia Radical

Sé audaz con ofertas y solicitudes: descubre lo que es posible cuando nos apoyamos mutuamente

Anclar la Abundancia

Da generosamente y confía en que colectivamente, tenemos recursos para que todos prosperen

"El viaje de tejer nuestra resiliencia nunca comienza ni termina. COhere es simplemente un ritmo que llama a prestar mayor atención a este proceso en el que todos participamos."

Ecosistema Regenerativo de Boulder

Junto con Climatique, creamos este mapa para demostrar el rico tapiz de proyectos y grupos que trabajan hacia el cambio regenerativo en nuestra comunidad.

Explora el Mapa
Sugerir Adiciones
Únete al Tejido

COhere es para todos los que se preocupan por el futuro de Boulder y quieren ser parte de crear una comunidad más conectada y resiliente.

Ya sea que participes en eventos, ofrezcas tus dones, o simplemente encarnes el espíritu de COhere en la vida diaria, eres parte de este tejido.

Facilitated by Ayleen Guzman of Mamafaeria Healing Arts At the center of this offering is the understanding that the Earth is not simply the place where we live, but a living spiritual presence that can become a gateway into connection with the Divine, the Divine Mother, God, our ancestors, and ourselves. The womb of the Earth can become a place of return, remembrance, healing, and transformation. We are living through profound and rapidly changing times. Across many Indigenous, African, Native, and spiritual traditions, there are teachings about periods of great transformation in which humanity is called to remember its relationship with the Earth and return to right relationship with one another. Within my own spiritual framework, this is a time when the Earth is calling us to become more sensitive to her presence, her needs, and the wisdom she carries. People of the Sacred Land (Film Screening + Dialogue)

17:30 – 19:30 GMT-6

Naropa Cultural Center · 2150 Arapahoe Ave · Boulder

The Untold History of Colorado The idea that we are living on stolen land isn’t new, or even novel; it’s a reality that exists across settler communities worldwide, and many people in the United States are aware of the blatant agendas, coercion, and profound immorality of the treaty process. What’s often missing from that conversation, however, are rigorous, comprehensive, academically supported Native-led studies proving that— even through the lens of modern law— large areas of what we call the United States remain illegally occupied. And nowhere is the evidence and culpability more dramatic than in the state of Colorado. PEOPLE of the SACRED LAND (2026, 32 min) follows Richard Willams (Oglala Lakota, Northern Cheyenne) as he recounts the findings of the Truth, Restoration, and Education Commission (TREC) of Colorado’s TREC Reports. While Rick’s story focuses on Colorado, the approach, implications, and impact of his work provide a model for Native leaders across the continent. Community Grief Ritual: Tending the Soil

18:00 – 21:00 GMT-6

Boulder

Facilitated by Danielle Rifkin, Dan Maynard, and Sarah (Naiya) D'Antoni of the Grief Collective. Positioned at the opening of Cohere week, this ritual seeds the soil for what the week will grow. Before we can plant connection, we have to grieve where we fractured: where we lost each other, where ruptures went unrepaired, where survival under capitalism pulled us away from each other, where we got severed from land. We grieve alone because we forgot how to grieve together. This ritual is a return to the village, a remembering that mourning was always meant to be collective. We'll work with song, story, and systemic constellations, drawing on ritual lineages from Joanna Macy, Francis Weller, Martin Prechtel, Malidoma Somé, and the Mythic Body.

People of the Sacred Land (Film Screening + Dialogue)

17:30 – 19:30 GMT-6

Naropa Cultural Center · 2150 Arapahoe Ave · Boulder

The Untold History of Colorado The idea that we are living on stolen land isn’t new, or even novel; it’s a reality that exists across settler communities worldwide, and many people in the United States are aware of the blatant agendas, coercion, and profound immorality of the treaty process. What’s often missing from that conversation, however, are rigorous, comprehensive, academically supported Native-led studies proving that— even through the lens of modern law— large areas of what we call the United States remain illegally occupied. And nowhere is the evidence and culpability more dramatic than in the state of Colorado. PEOPLE of the SACRED LAND (2026, 32 min) follows Richard Willams (Oglala Lakota, Northern Cheyenne) as he recounts the findings of the Truth, Restoration, and Education Commission (TREC) of Colorado’s TREC Reports. While Rick’s story focuses on Colorado, the approach, implications, and impact of his work provide a model for Native leaders across the continent. Richard Williams: Executive Producer Dewi: Director, cinematographer, editor Sarah Ortegon Highwalking: Field director Jason: Cinematographer, finishing editor

Community Grief Ritual: Tending the Soil

6:00 PM – 9:00 PM MDT

Boulder

Facilitated by Danielle Rifkin, Dan Maynard, and Sarah (Naiya) D'Antoni of the Grief Collective. Positioned at the opening of Cohere week, this ritual seeds the soil for what the week will grow. Before we can plant connection, we have to grieve where we fractured: where we lost each other, where ruptures went unrepaired, where survival under capitalism pulled us away from each other, where we got severed from land. We grieve alone because we forgot how to grieve together. This ritual is a return to the village, a remembering that mourning was always meant to be collective. We'll work with song, story, and systemic constellations, drawing on ritual lineages from Joanna Macy, Francis Weller, Martin Prechtel, Malidoma Somé, and the Mythic Body.

A Sound Healing Journey into the Womb of the Earth for Ecological Self-Restoration

8:00 AM – 9:30 AM MDT

Eben G Fine Park · Boulder

Facilitated by Ayleen Guzman of Mamafaeria Healing Arts At the center of this offering is the understanding that the Earth is not simply the place where we live, but a living spiritual presence that can become a gateway into connection with the Divine, the Divine Mother, God, our ancestors, and ourselves. The womb of the Earth can become a place of return, remembrance, healing, and transformation. We are living through profound and rapidly changing times. Across many Indigenous, African, Native, and spiritual traditions, there are teachings about periods of great transformation in which humanity is called to remember its relationship with the Earth and return to right relationship with one another. Within my own spiritual framework, this is a time when the Earth is calling us to become more sensitive to her presence, her needs, and the wisdom she carries. The intention of this ceremony is to begin cultivating that relationship consciously.

MONDAY, OCTOBER 19, 2026

People of the Sacred Land (Film Screening + Dialogue)

5:30 PM – 7:30 PM MDT

Naropa Cultural Center · 2150 Arapahoe Ave · Boulder

The Untold History of Colorado The idea that we are living on stolen land isn’t new, or even novel; it’s a reality that exists across settler communities worldwide, and many people in the United States are aware of the blatant agendas, coercion, and profound immorality of the treaty process. What’s often missing from that conversation, however, are rigorous, comprehensive, academically supported Native-led studies proving that— even through the lens of modern law— large areas of what we call the United States remain illegally occupied. And nowhere is the evidence and culpability more dramatic than in the state of Colorado. PEOPLE of the SACRED LAND (2026, 32 min) follows Richard Willams (Oglala Lakota, Northern Cheyenne) as he recounts the findings of the Truth, Restoration, and Education Commission (TREC) of Colorado’s TREC Reports. While Rick’s story focuses on Colorado, the approach, implications, and impact of his work provide a model for Native leaders across the continent. Richard Williams: Executive Producer Dewi: Director, cinematographer, editor Sarah Ortegon Highwalking: Field director Jason: Cinematographer, finishing editor

The Untold History of Colorado The idea that we are living on stolen land isn’t new, or even novel; it’s a reality that exists across settler communities worldwide, and many people in the United States are aware of the blatant agendas, coercion, and profound immorality of the treaty process. What’s often missing from that conversation, however, are rigorous, comprehensive, academically supported Native-led studies proving that— even through the lens of modern law— large areas of what we call the United States remain illegally occupied. And nowhere is the evidence and culpability more dramatic than in the state of Colorado. PEOPLE of the SACRED LAND (2026, 32 min) follows Richard Willams (Oglala Lakota, Northern Cheyenne) as he recounts the findings of the Truth, Restoration, and Education Commission (TREC) of Colorado’s TREC Reports. While Rick’s story focuses on Colorado, the approach, implications, and impact of his work provide a model for Native leaders across the continent. What is COhere?

COhere Boulder stokes Boulder's culture and engagement by connecting residents, organizations, artists, leaders, and innovators during a 10-day container. Through a curated calendar of values-aligned events and memorable opening & closing gatherings, we strengthen community ties, highlight our city's vibrancy, and inspire action toward a more regenerative, resilient future.

This isn't just another conference or workshop series. It's a carefully designed journey that helps our community discover its own resilience patterns, strengthen existing connections, and create new pathways for collaboration.

Building on the success of COhere 2024 and 2025, we're evolving into an annual rhythm that makes community participation memorable, meaningful, and accessible to all.

THIS YEAR'S THEME

We Are Our Ecology

The Community Calendar

Co-created by everyone who shows up

COhere doesn't program the ten days from the top down. Every event on the calendar is offered by someone in this community — a dinner, a walk, a workshop, a song circle, a conversation that needed a room.

Browse what's unfolding, and if you're holding something you'd like to share, there's room for it here.

Explore the Calendar
Co-create
Choose Your Own Adventure

There is no single way to do COhere. Ten days, a calendar the community builds together, and an open invitation to find your own thread through it.

Come to one gathering or a dozen. Host something. Bring a friend. Meet the people already tending what you care about — and find your role in the web.

Participate

We hope all participants build new relationships, learn meaningful things about Boulder, and find their role in the web.

Contribute

Share a story, host an event, volunteer, make art.

Lead

Get involved in the organizing team, or anchor an element of COhere that brings a dimension of community to life.

Experience COhere

See and feel what COhere is all about — films from our first two years

COhere Boulder

COhere 2024 Recap

Two years of weaving: hundreds of community members and dozens of co-created events across Boulder, strengthening connections and planting seeds for our regenerative future.

The Spirit of COhere
Active Participation

Life becomes more meaningful when we lean in, being courageously participatory

Radical Interdependence

Be bold with offers and requests—discover what's possible when we lean on each other

Anchor Abundance

Give generously and trust that collectively, we are resourced for all to thrive

"The journey of weaving our resilience never begins and never ends. COhere is simply a rhythm that calls deeper attention to this process in which we all engage."

Boulder's Regenerative Ecosystem

Together with Climatique, we created this map to demonstrate the rich tapestry of projects and groups working towards regenerative change in our community.

Explore the Map
Suggest Additions
Join the Weaving

COhere is for everyone who cares about Boulder's future and wants to be part of creating a more connected, resilient community.

Whether you participate in events, offer your gifts, or simply embody the spirit of COhere in daily life, you're part of this weaving.

FRIDAY, OCTOBER 16, 2026

Community Grief Ritual: Tending the Soil

6:00 PM – 9:00 PM MDT

Boulder

Facilitated by Danielle Rifkin, Dan Maynard, and Sarah (Naiya) D'Antoni of the Grief Collective. Positioned at the opening of Cohere week, this ritual seeds the soil for what the week will grow. Before we can plant connection, we have to grieve where we fractured: where we lost each other, where ruptures went unrepaired, where survival under capitalism pulled us away from each other, where we got severed from land. We grieve alone because we forgot how to grieve together. This ritual is a return to the village, a remembering that mourning was always meant to be collective. We'll work with song, story, and systemic constellations, drawing on ritual lineages from Joanna Macy, Francis Weller, Martin Prechtel, Malidoma Somé, and the Mythic Body.

High Plains Environmental Center · 2698 Bluestem Willow Dr · Loveland

A mindful birding walk combines traditional birdwatching with mindfulness techniques, focusing on slow-paced, intentional awareness of birds and nature. Observing birds in their natural habitat can be inspiring and relaxing while also offering a variety of health benefits. This way of connecting with nature encourages purposeful curiosity, builds community, and deepens our appreciation for birds and the natural world. Join us at the High Plains Environmental Center to explore mindfulness and birds and learn simple techniques you can take home and practice on your own. We’ll begin in the classroom and then head outside for a guided walk. All abilities and interests are welcome! We'll provide bird books and binoculars. Please dress appropriately for the weather. Boulder

Facilitated by Danielle Rifkin, Dan Maynard, and Sarah (Naiya) D'Antoni of the Grief Collective. Positioned at the opening of Cohere week, this ritual seeds the soil for what the week will grow. Before we can plant connection, we have to grieve where we fractured: where we lost each other, where ruptures went unrepaired, where survival under capitalism pulled us away from each other, where we got severed from land. We grieve alone because we forgot how to grieve together. This ritual is a return to the village, a remembering that mourning was always meant to be collective. We'll work with song, story, and systemic constellations, drawing on ritual lineages from Joanna Macy, Francis Weller, Martin Prechtel, Malidoma Somé, and the Mythic Body.

People of the Sacred Land (Film Screening + Dialogue)

17:30 – 19:30 GMT-6

Naropa Cultural Center · 2150 Arapahoe Ave · Boulder

The Untold History of Colorado The idea that we are living on stolen land isn’t new, or even novel; it’s a reality that exists across settler communities worldwide, and many people in the United States are aware of the blatant agendas, coercion, and profound immorality of the treaty process. What’s often missing from that conversation, however, are rigorous, comprehensive, academically supported Native-led studies proving that— even through the lens of modern law— large areas of what we call the United States remain illegally occupied. And nowhere is the evidence and culpability more dramatic than in the state of Colorado. PEOPLE of the SACRED LAND (2026, 32 min) follows Richard Willams (Oglala Lakota, Northern Cheyenne) as he recounts the findings of the Truth, Restoration, and Education Commission (TREC) of Colorado’s TREC Reports. While Rick’s story focuses on Colorado, the approach, implications, and impact of his work provide a model for Native leaders across the continent. Richard Williams: Executive Producer Dewi: Director, cinematographer, editor Sarah Ortegon Highwalking: Field director Jason: Cinematographer, finishing editor

17:30 – 19:30 GMT-6

Naropa Cultural Center · 2150 Arapahoe Ave · Boulder

The Untold History of Colorado The idea that we are living on stolen land isn’t new, or even novel; it’s a reality that exists across settler communities worldwide, and many people in the United States are aware of the blatant agendas, coercion, and profound immorality of the treaty process. What’s often missing from that conversation, however, are rigorous, comprehensive, academically supported Native-led studies proving that— even through the lens of modern law— large areas of what we call the United States remain illegally occupied. And nowhere is the evidence and culpability more dramatic than in the state of Colorado. PEOPLE of the SACRED LAND (2026, 32 min) follows Richard Willams (Oglala Lakota, Northern Cheyenne) as he recounts the findings of the Truth, Restoration, and Education Commission (TREC) of Colorado’s TREC Reports. While Rick’s story focuses on Colorado, the approach, implications, and impact of his work provide a model for Native leaders across the continent. ¿Qué es COhere?

COhere Boulder aviva la cultura y el compromiso de Boulder conectando residentes, organizaciones, artistas, líderes e innovadores durante un contenedor de 10 días. A través de un calendario curado de eventos alineados con valores y reuniones memorables de apertura y cierre, fortalecemos los lazos comunitarios, destacamos la vitalidad de nuestra ciudad e inspiramos acción hacia un futuro más regenerativo y resiliente.

Esto no es solo otra conferencia o serie de talleres. Es un viaje cuidadosamente diseñado que ayuda a nuestra comunidad a descubrir sus propios patrones de resiliencia, fortalecer las conexiones existentes y crear nuevos caminos para la colaboración.

Basándonos en el éxito de COhere 2024 y 2025, estamos evolucionando hacia un ritmo anual que hace que la participación comunitaria sea memorable, significativa y accesible para todos.

EL TEMA DE ESTE AÑO

Somos Nuestra Ecología

El calendario comunitario

Co-creado por todas las personas que participan

COhere no programa los diez días desde arriba. Cada evento del calendario es ofrecido por alguien de esta comunidad: una cena, una caminata, un taller, un círculo de canto, una conversación que necesitaba un espacio.

Explora lo que se está desplegando y, si tienes algo que quieras compartir, aquí hay espacio para ello.

Explorar el Calendario
Co-crear
Elige Tu Propia Aventura

No hay una sola manera de vivir COhere. Diez días, un calendario que la comunidad construye en conjunto y una invitación abierta a encontrar tu propio hilo.

Ven a un encuentro o a doce. Organiza algo. Trae a alguien. Conoce a las personas que ya cuidan lo que te importa y encuentra tu lugar en la red.

Participa

Esperamos que todas las personas participantes creen nuevas relaciones, aprendan cosas significativas sobre Boulder y encuentren su lugar en la red.

Contribuye

Comparte una historia, organiza un evento, ofrece tu tiempo, crea arte.

Lidera

Súmate al equipo organizador o ancla un elemento de COhere que dé vida a una dimensión de la comunidad.

Experimenta COhere

Mira y siente de qué se trata COhere — películas de nuestros primeros dos años

COhere Boulder

Resumen de COhere 2024

Dos años de tejido: cientos de miembros de la comunidad y docenas de eventos co-creados en todo Boulder, fortaleciendo conexiones y plantando semillas para nuestro futuro regenerativo.

El Espíritu de COhere
Participación Activa

La vida se vuelve más significativa cuando nos involucramos, siendo valientemente participativos

Interdependencia Radical

Sé audaz con ofertas y solicitudes: descubre lo que es posible cuando nos apoyamos mutuamente

Anclar la Abundancia

Da generosamente y confía en que colectivamente, tenemos recursos para que todos prosperen

"El viaje de tejer nuestra resiliencia nunca comienza ni termina. COhere es simplemente un ritmo que llama a prestar mayor atención a este proceso en el que todos participamos."

Ecosistema Regenerativo de Boulder

Junto con Climatique, creamos este mapa para demostrar el rico tapiz de proyectos y grupos que trabajan hacia el cambio regenerativo en nuestra comunidad.

Explora el Mapa
Sugerir Adiciones
Únete al Tejido

COhere es para todos los que se preocupan por el futuro de Boulder y quieren ser parte de crear una comunidad más conectada y resiliente.

Ya sea que participes en eventos, ofrezcas tus dones, o simplemente encarnes el espíritu de COhere en la vida diaria, eres parte de este tejido.

¿Qué es COhere?

COhere Boulder aviva la cultura y el compromiso de Boulder conectando residentes, organizaciones, artistas, líderes e innovadores durante un contenedor de 10 días. A través de un calendario curado de eventos alineados con valores y reuniones memorables de apertura y cierre, fortalecemos los lazos comunitarios, destacamos la vitalidad de nuestra ciudad e inspiramos acción hacia un futuro más regenerativo y resiliente.

Esto no es solo otra conferencia o serie de talleres. Es un viaje cuidadosamente diseñado que ayuda a nuestra comunidad a descubrir sus propios patrones de resiliencia, fortalecer las conexiones existentes y crear nuevos caminos para la colaboración.

Basándonos en el éxito de COhere 2024 y 2025, estamos evolucionando hacia un ritmo anual que hace que la participación comunitaria sea memorable, significativa y accesible para todos.

EL TEMA DE ESTE AÑO

Somos Nuestra Ecología

El calendario comunitario

Co-creado por todas las personas que participan

COhere no programa los diez días desde arriba. Cada evento del calendario es ofrecido por alguien de esta comunidad: una cena, una caminata, un taller, un círculo de canto, una conversación que necesitaba un espacio.

Explora lo que se está desplegando y, si tienes algo que quieras compartir, aquí hay espacio para ello.

Explorar el Calendario
Co-crear
Elige Tu Propia Aventura

No hay una sola manera de vivir COhere. Diez días, un calendario que la comunidad construye en conjunto y una invitación abierta a encontrar tu propio hilo.

Ven a un encuentro o a doce. Organiza algo. Trae a alguien. Conoce a las personas que ya cuidan lo que te importa y encuentra tu lugar en la red.

Participa

Esperamos que todas las personas participantes creen nuevas relaciones, aprendan cosas significativas sobre Boulder y encuentren su lugar en la red.

Contribuye

Comparte una historia, organiza un evento, ofrece tu tiempo, crea arte.

Lidera

Súmate al equipo organizador o ancla un elemento de COhere que dé vida a una dimensión de la comunidad.

Experimenta COhere

Mira y siente de qué se trata COhere — películas de nuestros primeros dos años

COhere Boulder

Resumen de COhere 2024

Dos años de tejido: cientos de miembros de la comunidad y docenas de eventos co-creados en todo Boulder, fortaleciendo conexiones y plantando semillas para nuestro futuro regenerativo.

El Espíritu de COhere
Participación Activa

La vida se vuelve más significativa cuando nos involucramos, siendo valientemente participativos

Interdependencia Radical

Sé audaz con ofertas y solicitudes: descubre lo que es posible cuando nos apoyamos mutuamente

Anclar la Abundancia

Da generosamente y confía en que colectivamente, tenemos recursos para que todos prosperen

"El viaje de tejer nuestra resiliencia nunca comienza ni termina. COhere es simplemente un ritmo que llama a prestar mayor atención a este proceso en el que todos participamos."

Ecosistema Regenerativo de Boulder

Junto con Climatique, creamos este mapa para demostrar el rico tapiz de proyectos y grupos que trabajan hacia el cambio regenerativo en nuestra comunidad.

Explora el Mapa

COhere es para todos los que se preocupan por el futuro de Boulder y quieren ser parte de crear una comunidad más conectada y resiliente.

Ya sea que participes en eventos, ofrezcas tus dones, o simplemente encarnes el espíritu de COhere en la vida diaria, eres parte de este tejido.

A Sound Healing Journey into the Womb of the Earth for Ecological Self-Restoration

8:00 – 9:30 GMT-6

Eben G Fine Park · Boulder

Facilitated by Ayleen Guzman of Mamafaeria Healing Arts At the center of this offering is the understanding that the Earth is not simply the place where we live, but a living spiritual presence that can become a gateway into connection with the Divine, the Divine Mother, God, our ancestors, and ourselves. The womb of the Earth can become a place of return, remembrance, healing, and transformation. We are living through profound and rapidly changing times. Across many Indigenous, African, Native, and spiritual traditions, there are teachings about periods of great transformation in which humanity is called to remember its relationship with the Earth and return to right relationship with one another. Within my own spiritual framework, this is a time when the Earth is calling us to become more sensitive to her presence, her needs, and the wisdom she carries. The intention of this ceremony is to begin cultivating that relationship consciously.

LUNES, 19 DE OCTUBRE DE 2026

People of the Sacred Land (Film Screening + Dialogue)

17:30 – 19:30 GMT-6

Naropa Cultural Center · 2150 Arapahoe Ave · Boulder

The Untold History of Colorado The idea that we are living on stolen land isn’t new, or even novel; it’s a reality that exists across settler communities worldwide, and many people in the United States are aware of the blatant agendas, coercion, and profound immorality of the treaty process. What’s often missing from that conversation, however, are rigorous, comprehensive, academically supported Native-led studies proving that— even through the lens of modern law— large areas of what we call the United States remain illegally occupied. And nowhere is the evidence and culpability more dramatic than in the state of Colorado. PEOPLE of the SACRED LAND (2026, 32 min) follows Richard Willams (Oglala Lakota, Northern Cheyenne) as he recounts the findings of the Truth, Restoration, and Education Commission (TREC) of Colorado’s TREC Reports. While Rick’s story focuses on Colorado, the approach, implications, and impact of his work provide a model for Native leaders across the continent. Richard Williams: Executive Producer Dewi: Director, cinematographer, editor Sarah Ortegon Highwalking: Field director Jason: Cinematographer, finishing editor

People of the Sacred Land (Film Screening + Dialogue)

17:30 – 19:30 GMT-6

Naropa Cultural Center · 2150 Arapahoe Ave · Boulder

The Untold History of Colorado The idea that we are living on stolen land isn’t new, or even novel; it’s a reality that exists across settler communities worldwide, and many people in the United States are aware of the blatant agendas, coercion, and profound immorality of the treaty process. What’s often missing from that conversation, however, are rigorous, comprehensive, academically supported Native-led studies proving that— even through the lens of modern law— large areas of what we call the United States remain illegally occupied. And nowhere is the evidence and culpability more dramatic than in the state of Colorado. PEOPLE of the SACRED LAND (2026, 32 min) follows Richard Willams (Oglala Lakota, Northern Cheyenne) as he recounts the findings of the Truth, Restoration, and Education Commission (TREC) of Colorado’s TREC Reports. While Rick’s story focuses on Colorado, the approach, implications, and impact of his work provide a model for Native leaders across the continent. Community Grief Ritual: Tending the Soil

6:00 PM – 9:00 PM MDT

Boulder

Facilitated by Danielle Rifkin, Dan Maynard, and Sarah (Naiya) D'Antoni of the Grief Collective. Positioned at the opening of Cohere week, this ritual seeds the soil for what the week will grow. Before we can plant connection, we have to grieve where we fractured: where we lost each other, where ruptures went unrepaired, where survival under capitalism pulled us away from each other, where we got severed from land. We grieve alone because we forgot how to grieve together. This ritual is a return to the village, a remembering that mourning was always meant to be collective. We'll work with song, story, and systemic constellations, drawing on ritual lineages from Joanna Macy, Francis Weller, Martin Prechtel, Malidoma Somé, and the Mythic Body.

FRIDAY, OCTOBER 16, 2026

Community Grief Ritual: Tending the Soil

6:00 PM – 9:00 PM MDT

Boulder

Facilitated by Danielle Rifkin, Dan Maynard, and Sarah (Naiya) D'Antoni of the Grief Collective. Positioned at the opening of Cohere week, this ritual seeds the soil for what the week will grow. Before we can plant connection, we have to grieve where we fractured: where we lost each other, where ruptures went unrepaired, where survival under capitalism pulled us away from each other, where we got severed from land. We grieve alone because we forgot how to grieve together. This ritual is a return to the village, a remembering that mourning was always meant to be collective. We'll work with song, story, and systemic constellations, drawing on ritual lineages from Joanna Macy, Francis Weller, Martin Prechtel, Malidoma Somé, and the Mythic Body.

A mindful birding walk combines traditional birdwatching with mindfulness techniques, focusing on slow-paced, intentional awareness of birds and nature. This way of connecting with nature encourages purposeful curiosity, builds community, and deepens our appreciation for birds and the natural world. What is COhere?

COhere Boulder stokes Boulder's culture and engagement by connecting residents, organizations, artists, leaders, and innovators during a 10-day container. Through a curated calendar of values-aligned events and memorable opening & closing gatherings, we strengthen community ties, highlight our city's vibrancy, and inspire action toward a more regenerative, resilient future.

This isn't just another conference or workshop series. It's a carefully designed journey that helps our community discover its own resilience patterns, strengthen existing connections, and create new pathways for collaboration.

Building on the success of COhere 2024 and 2025, we're evolving into an annual rhythm that makes community participation memorable, meaningful, and accessible to all.

THIS YEAR'S THEME

We Are Our Ecology

The Community Calendar

Co-created by everyone who shows up

COhere doesn't program the ten days from the top down. Every event on the calendar is offered by someone in this community — a dinner, a walk, a workshop, a song circle, a conversation that needed a room.

Browse what's unfolding, and if you're holding something you'd like to share, there's room for it here.

Explore the Calendar
Co-create
Choose Your Own Adventure

There is no single way to do COhere. Ten days, a calendar the community builds together, and an open invitation to find your own thread through it.

Come to one gathering or a dozen. Host something. Bring a friend. Meet the people already tending what you care about — and find your role in the web.

Participate

We hope all participants build new relationships, learn meaningful things about Boulder, and find their role in the web.

Contribute

Share a story, host an event, volunteer, make art.

Lead

Get involved in the organizing team, or anchor an element of COhere that brings a dimension of community to life.

Experience COhere

See and feel what COhere is all about — films from our first two years

COhere Boulder

COhere 2024 Recap

Two years of weaving: hundreds of community members and dozens of co-created events across Boulder, strengthening connections and planting seeds for our regenerative future.

The Spirit of COhere
Active Participation

Life becomes more meaningful when we lean in, being courageously participatory

Radical Interdependence

Be bold with offers and requests—discover what's possible when we lean on each other

Anchor Abundance

Give generously and trust that collectively, we are resourced for all to thrive

"The journey of weaving our resilience never begins and never ends. COhere is simply a rhythm that calls deeper attention to this process in which we all engage."

Boulder's Regenerative Ecosystem

Together with Climatique, we created this map to demonstrate the rich tapestry of projects and groups working towards regenerative change in our community.

Explore the Map
Suggest Additions
Join the Weaving

COhere is for everyone who cares about Boulder's future and wants to be part of creating a more connected, resilient community.

Whether you participate in events, offer your gifts, or simply embody the spirit of COhere in daily life, you're part of this weaving.

8:00 AM – 9:30 AM MDT

The womb of the Earth can become a place of return, remembrance, healing, and transformation. We are living through profound and rapidly changing times. Across many Indigenous, African, Native, and spiritual traditions, there are teachings about periods of great transformation in which humanity is called to remember its relationship with the Earth and return to right relationship with one another. People of the Sacred Land (Film Screening + Dialogue)

5:30 PM – 7:30 PM MDT

Naropa Cultural Center · 2150 Arapahoe Ave · Boulder

The Untold History of Colorado The idea that we are living on stolen land isn’t new, or even novel; it’s a reality that exists across settler communities worldwide, and many people in the United States are aware of the blatant agendas, coercion, and profound immorality of the treaty process. What’s often missing from that conversation, however, are rigorous, comprehensive, academically supported Native-led studies proving that— even through the lens of modern law— large areas of what we call the United States remain illegally occupied. And nowhere is the evidence and culpability more dramatic than in the state of Colorado. PEOPLE of the SACRED LAND (2026, 32 min) follows Richard Willams (Oglala Lakota, Northern Cheyenne) as he recounts the findings of the Truth, Restoration, and Education Commission (TREC) of Colorado’s TREC Reports. While Rick’s story focuses on Colorado, the approach, implications, and impact of his work provide a model for Native leaders across the continent. Community Grief Ritual: Tending the Soil

Boulder

Facilitated by Danielle Rifkin, Dan Maynard, and Sarah (Naiya) D'Antoni of the Grief Collective. Positioned at the opening of Cohere week, this ritual seeds the soil for what the week will grow. Before we can plant connection, we have to grieve where we fractured: where we lost each other, where ruptures went unrepaired, where survival under capitalism pulled us away from each other, where we got severed from land. We grieve alone because we forgot how to grieve together. This ritual is a return to the village, a remembering that mourning was always meant to be collective. We'll work with song, story, and systemic constellations, drawing on ritual lineages from Joanna Macy, Francis Weller, Martin Prechtel, Malidoma Somé, and the Mythic Body.

People of the Sacred Land (Film Screening + Dialogue)

5:30 PM – 7:30 PM MDT

Naropa Cultural Center · 2150 Arapahoe Ave · Boulder

The Untold History of Colorado The idea that we are living on stolen land isn’t new, or even novel; it’s a reality that exists across settler communities worldwide, and many people in the United States are aware of the blatant agendas, coercion, and profound immorality of the treaty process. What’s often missing from that conversation, however, are rigorous, comprehensive, academically supported Native-led studies proving that— even through the lens of modern law— large areas of what we call the United States remain illegally occupied. And nowhere is the evidence and culpability more dramatic than in the state of Colorado. PEOPLE of the SACRED LAND (2026, 32 min) follows Richard Willams (Oglala Lakota, Northern Cheyenne) as he recounts the findings of the Truth, Restoration, and Education Commission (TREC) of Colorado’s TREC Reports. While Rick’s story focuses on Colorado, the approach, implications, and impact of his work provide a model for Native leaders across the continent. Richard Williams: Executive Producer Dewi: Director, cinematographer, editor Sarah Ortegon Highwalking: Field director Jason: Cinematographer, finishing editor

Community Grief Ritual: Tending the Soil

18:00 – 21:00 GMT-6

Boulder

Facilitated by Danielle Rifkin, Dan Maynard, and Sarah (Naiya) D'Antoni of the Grief Collective. Positioned at the opening of Cohere week, this ritual seeds the soil for what the week will grow. Before we can plant connection, we have to grieve where we fractured: where we lost each other, where ruptures went unrepaired, where survival under capitalism pulled us away from each other, where we got severed from land. We grieve alone because we forgot how to grieve together. This ritual is a return to the village, a remembering that mourning was always meant to be collective. We'll work with song, story, and systemic constellations, drawing on ritual lineages from Joanna Macy, Francis Weller, Martin Prechtel, Malidoma Somé, and the Mythic Body.

¿Qué es COhere?

COhere Boulder aviva la cultura y el compromiso de Boulder conectando residentes, organizaciones, artistas, líderes e innovadores durante un contenedor de 10 días. A través de un calendario curado de eventos alineados con valores y reuniones memorables de apertura y cierre, fortalecemos los lazos comunitarios, destacamos la vitalidad de nuestra ciudad e inspiramos acción hacia un futuro más regenerativo y resiliente.

Esto no es solo otra conferencia o serie de talleres. Es un viaje cuidadosamente diseñado que ayuda a nuestra comunidad a descubrir sus propios patrones de resiliencia, fortalecer las conexiones existentes y crear nuevos caminos para la colaboración.

Basándonos en el éxito de COhere 2024 y 2025, estamos evolucionando hacia un ritmo anual que hace que la participación comunitaria sea memorable, significativa y accesible para todos.

EL TEMA DE ESTE AÑO

Somos Nuestra Ecología

El calendario comunitario

Co-creado por todas las personas que participan

COhere no programa los diez días desde arriba. Cada evento del calendario es ofrecido por alguien de esta comunidad: una cena, una caminata, un taller, un círculo de canto, una conversación que necesitaba un espacio.

Explora lo que se está desplegando y, si tienes algo que quieras compartir, aquí hay espacio para ello.

Explorar el Calendario
Co-crear
Elige Tu Propia Aventura

No hay una sola manera de vivir COhere. Diez días, un calendario que la comunidad construye en conjunto y una invitación abierta a encontrar tu propio hilo.

Ven a un encuentro o a doce. Organiza algo. Trae a alguien. Conoce a las personas que ya cuidan lo que te importa y encuentra tu lugar en la red.

Participa

Esperamos que todas las personas participantes creen nuevas relaciones, aprendan cosas significativas sobre Boulder y encuentren su lugar en la red.

Contribuye

Comparte una historia, organiza un evento, ofrece tu tiempo, crea arte.

Lidera

Súmate al equipo organizador o ancla un elemento de COhere que dé vida a una dimensión de la comunidad.

Experimenta COhere

Mira y siente de qué se trata COhere — películas de nuestros primeros dos años

COhere Boulder

Resumen de COhere 2024

Dos años de tejido: cientos de miembros de la comunidad y docenas de eventos co-creados en todo Boulder, fortaleciendo conexiones y plantando semillas para nuestro futuro regenerativo.

El Espíritu de COhere
Participación Activa

La vida se vuelve más significativa cuando nos involucramos, siendo valientemente participativos

Interdependencia Radical

Sé audaz con ofertas y solicitudes: descubre lo que es posible cuando nos apoyamos mutuamente

Anclar la Abundancia

Da generosamente y confía en que colectivamente, tenemos recursos para que todos prosperen

"El viaje de tejer nuestra resiliencia nunca comienza ni termina. COhere es simplemente un ritmo que llama a prestar mayor atención a este proceso en el que todos participamos."

Ecosistema Regenerativo de Boulder

Junto con Climatique, creamos este mapa para demostrar el rico tapiz de proyectos y grupos que trabajan hacia el cambio regenerativo en nuestra comunidad.

Explora el Mapa
Sugerir Adiciones
Únete al Tejido

COhere es para todos los que se preocupan por el futuro de Boulder y quieren ser parte de crear una comunidad más conectada y resiliente.

Ya sea que participes en eventos, ofrezcas tus dones, o simplemente encarnes el espíritu de COhere en la vida diaria, eres parte de este tejido.

A mindful birding walk combines traditional birdwatching with mindfulness techniques, focusing on slow-paced, intentional awareness of birds and nature. This way of connecting with nature encourages purposeful curiosity, builds community, and deepens our appreciation for birds and the natural world. Community Grief Ritual: Tending the Soil

18:00 – 21:00 GMT-6

Boulder

Facilitated by Danielle Rifkin, Dan Maynard, and Sarah (Naiya) D'Antoni of the Grief Collective. Positioned at the opening of Cohere week, this ritual seeds the soil for what the week will grow. Before we can plant connection, we have to grieve where we fractured: where we lost each other, where ruptures went unrepaired, where survival under capitalism pulled us away from each other, where we got severed from land. We grieve alone because we forgot how to grieve together. This ritual is a return to the village, a remembering that mourning was always meant to be collective. We'll work with song, story, and systemic constellations, drawing on ritual lineages from Joanna Macy, Francis Weller, Martin Prechtel, Malidoma Somé, and the Mythic Body.

Facilitated by Ayleen Guzman of Mamafaeria Healing Arts At the center of this offering is the understanding that the Earth is not simply the place where we live, but a living spiritual presence that can become a gateway into connection with the Divine, the Divine Mother, God, our ancestors, and ourselves. The womb of the Earth can become a place of return, remembrance, healing, and transformation. We are living through profound and rapidly changing times. Across many Indigenous, African, Native, and spiritual traditions, there are teachings about periods of great transformation in which humanity is called to remember its relationship with the Earth and return to right relationship with one another. Within my own spiritual framework, this is a time when the Earth is calling us to become more sensitive to her presence, her needs, and the wisdom she carries. The intention of this ceremony is to begin cultivating that relationship consciously.
